{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOV5s7_c8AAAABiAMZ9Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bs-hLzhLX8qQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bs-hL", "number": 1, "title": "Establish collaboration and review guidelines", "body": "## Goal

Establish the contribution workflow and documentation for nes-rust-neo, an experimental NES emulator project in Rust. Make the workflow usable by contributors and ProjectWeave from the first change. This task covers documentation and GitHub templates.

## Deliverables

- Add a `README.md` that states the project's purpose and its current development status and links to the contribution guidance.
- Add a short `AGENTS.md` that points contributors and coding agents to `docs/development-flow.md` and `docs/review-guidelines.md`.
- Document the workflow on `main` from Issue through implementation, PR, review, merge, and Issue closure. Use English for new collaboration documents, Issue and PR text, reviews, and commit messages.
- Add a GitHub Issue template that asks for scope, concrete pre-merge acceptance criteria, and any required post-merge verification. Add a PR template that records the source Issue, what changed, validation results, and any pending post-merge verification.

## Review and completion rules

- Define required pre-merge criteria that an agent can verify directly by default. Require human confirmation only when the Issue explains why it is necessary before merge. Tie blocking review findings to the Issue's scope and include concrete evidence and a way to verify the fix. Record unrelated improvements as follow-up work.
- Use `Closes #N` when the PR fully satisfies the Issue's requirements and mandatory pre-merge checks. Link intentionally partial work without closing the Issue, and state what remains.
- When a check is possible only after publication, merge the otherwise complete PR and close the original Issue first. Then perform and record the verification. Open a new Issue if it reveals a defect.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- All listed files exist, agree on the workflow and completion rules, and link to the relevant guidance.
- Relative links and Markdown anchors resolve, the Issue template has valid YAML front matter, and `git diff --check` passes. Record the checks performed in the PR.

## Post-merge verification
